comments.author: grinem
goutham-valugula
comments.text: I checked the current implementation: the root payload builder skips only `undefined`, so an explicit `null` for `description` or `activeVersionId` is serialized and changes the hash. One detail to pin down before treating null as equivalent to missing: these fields are typed `string | null`, so does the workflow persistence/API layer guarantee that `null` means “unset” for both? If so, normalizing null at this top-level field loop would address the reported case without changing nested null handling; otherwise the checksum may be preserving a meaningful cleared value.

comments.author: grinem
comments.text:
In the API and export serialization layers, missing keys and explicit `null` are already treated the same way for root workflow metadata (both map to empty/null states in TypeORM without functional differences).

Handling it right in the root checksum loop makes sense so we don't break nested node parameters, where `null` could actually be intentional user input:

```ts
// In the root checksum serializer loop:
if (value === undefined || (isRootMetadataField(key) && value === null)) continue;
```

Restricting the normalization to top-level metadata fields like `description` should resolve the hash mismatch cleanly without unexpected side effects.

comments.author: Arin004joshi
comments.text:
> The mismatch happens because `undefined` properties are omitted during `JSON.stringify`, while explicit `null` values serialize into the payload string and produce a different SHA-256 hash.
> 
> Since `null` and `undefined` represent the absence of a value for nullable top-level fields in `WORKFLOW_CHECKSUM_FIELDS`, filtering both at the root payload builder keeps the checksum consistent.
>

> 
> **Patch Preview (First 3 lines of verified fix):**
> 
> for (const field of WORKFLOW_CHECKSUM_FIELDS) {
> 	const value = workflow[field];
> 	if (value != null) {
> # ... [TRUNCATED — Full production patch & verification steps locked below]

Hey @grinem, I've gone through the issue and implemented a fix locally. I had one question regarding the implementation approach.

In `packages/workflow/src/workflow-checksum.ts`, I've introduced the following:

```typescript
type WorkflowChecksumField = (typeof WORKFLOW_CHECKSUM_FIELDS)[number];

/**
 * Fields that are nullable on `WorkflowSnapshot`. For these fields `null` has
 * the same meaning as `undefined`: the value is absent. For all other fields
 * `null` is a meaningful value and must stay in the checksum payload.
 */
const NULLABLE_CHECKSUM_FIELDS: ReadonlySet<WorkflowChecksumField> = new Set([
    'description',
    'activeVersionId',
]);
```

Since `WorkflowSnapshot` already declares the nullable fields through its TypeScript types, would you prefer keeping this explicit `ReadonlySet`, or is there an existing convention or a better way to derive this information without maintaining two separate sources of truth?

I'd appreciate your thoughts on which approach would be more appropriate here.

comments.author: goutham-valugula
comments.text: There is a similar pattern in `schemas.ts`: `optionalNonNullableINodeKeys` is derived from the Zod shape, so the schema stays the source of truth. `WorkflowSnapshot` currently has only a TypeScript interface, though, and its types are erased at runtime. Unless this checksum input gets a runtime schema, an explicit set for the nullable checksum fields seems reasonable; deriving the set from the type alone is not possible at runtime.

Thanks for clarifying! That makes sense. Since `WorkflowSnapshot` is only a TypeScript interface and doesn't provide runtime metadata, I'll keep the explicit `ReadonlySet` for the nullable checksum fields. This also keeps the normalization scoped to the fields where `null` represents an absent value.
I'll go ahead and raise the PR.

comments.author: grinem
Arin004joshi
comments.text:
> Since TypeScript types are erased at compile time, you can't introspect `WorkflowSnapshot` at runtime without a runtime schema or decorator metadata, which `packages/workflow` doesn't use here. An explicit runtime set or tuple is the standard way to handle this in n8n.
> 
> To prevent the set from drifting out of sync with the type definition, you can enforce compile-time safety by typing the keys against nullable snapshot properties:
> 
> type NullableKeys<T> = {
> 	[K in keyof T]: null extends T[K] ? K : never;
> }[keyof T];
> 
> type NullableChecksumField = Extract<WorkflowChecksumField, NullableKeys<WorkflowSnapshot>>;
> 
> const NULLABLE_CHECKSUM_FIELDS: ReadonlySet<NullableChecksumField> = new Set([
> 	'description',
> 	'activeVersionId',
> ]);
> That said, it's worth checking whether `null` and `undefined` ever have distinct semantic meanings for _any_ field currently in `WORKFLOW_CHECKSUM_FIELDS`. If all checksummed fields treat explicit `null` and omitted (`undefined`) as equivalent absent states, handling `value != null` across all fields would eliminate the need to maintain a separate list altogether. sorry for the delay

Hey @grinem. No worries about the delay, and thanks for taking the time to review this.

I've also opened a PR with the fix here: <https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/pull/44760>

I kept the explicit `ReadonlySet<WorkflowChecksumField>` containing just `description` and `activeVersionId`. I checked all ten fields in `WORKFLOW_CHECKSUM_FIELDS`: those are the only two declared `| null`. I did not switch to `value != null` for all fields, because `meta` is typed `unknown` (`null extends unknown` is true), so a global filter would also drop a legitimate root-level `meta: null` and broaden the change beyond the reported issue.

I also looked at the `NullableKeys` guard you suggested. With the current `WorkflowSnapshot`, it would evaluate to `'description' | 'activeVersionId' | 'meta'` because `meta?: unknown`, and it only rejects invalid keys — it would not force us to add a newly nullable field later. Given that, I left it out to keep the change minimal, but I'm happy to add it (with `unknown` excluded) if you'd prefer the compile-time guard.

Does the current approach look good to you, or would you like any changes before this can move forward?
